resolution_rationale: This review provisionally assesses the two required aspects against the attached implementation. It does not resolve the existing issues: no correlated execution or checker was supplied, and the additional source preserves the protective paths and outstanding scheduling conditions.

items.rationale: The obligation has an explicit, scoped producer-consumer justification beyond protocol naming. The recovery threshold writes both lb.cmds and inst.cmds, marks the instance ACCEPTED, and publishes those commands through bcastAccept. Matching acceptance replies can then commit that instance without checking its contents against an earlier decision; executeCommands consumes its commands at the corresponding execution position. PUT and NOOP have different state effects. Preserving an independently supported decision at this publication boundary is therefore a reasonable inferred implementation responsibility, rather than a requirement to preserve every accepted proposal. The constructor enables execution, the run loop dispatches recovery without a leadership guard, and recovery creates nil-client bookkeeping when the nonleader has none. At N=3 and F=1, both relevant thresholds are two. These sources support applicability under the declared premises, but do not establish that those premises and the assignment occur in one legal execution.
counterevidence: The README identifies classic Paxos but does not explicitly specify command equality at this internal assignment; the expectation remains an attributed producer-consumer inference.
A committed participant answers Prepare with full Commit information. handleAccept protects committed instances and rejects lower ballots, potentially preventing a conflicting continuation.

items.rationale: The decomposition correctly separates the prior supported decision, recovery assignment, subsequent commitment and application. An independently retained snapshot must include ordered command contents and value bytes because recovery replaces mutable instance fields. Distinct installation witnesses are necessary: handleAccept replies even on branches that reject or preserve an existing instance, so a matching ballot or counter alone does not establish acceptance of the proposed commands. The selected bindings cover bookkeeping creation, assignment, publication, installation, decision and execution consumption. Satisfying this obligation excludes replacement at the selected recovery boundary only. Broader disagreement could still arise through other command replacement paths, reply accounting or commit processing while this obligation holds. Conversely, commit information or acceptance rejection could prevent a conflicting decision after an assignment mismatch. The narrower obligation and separate consequence witnesses therefore remain appropriate.
counterevidence: Full Commit responses and committed-instance acceptance protection can stop a continuation without establishing preservation at the assignment itself.
The prepare-threshold branch leaves vbal unchanged; behavior must not silently equate it with bal.
handlePrepareReply has no committed-status guard and does not reset prepareOKs after threshold passage. Later authentic replies can trigger further assignments.
recover does not recheck committed status before preparing, so a queued recovery request cannot automatically be discarded when commit information arrives.
Preserving every previously accepted value would impose a stronger requirement than the supported-decision premise.
